Original Requirements: Build a simple todo list application with add, delete, and mark complete features
Product Goals: Provide a user-friendly interface for managing tasks.
Ensure data persistence to prevent data loss.
Offer a responsive design accessible across devices.
User Stories: As a user, I want to be able to add new tasks to my todo list.
As a user, I want to be able to delete tasks from my todo list.
As a user, I want to be able to mark tasks as complete.
As a user, I want my todo list to be saved so I can access it later.
As a user, I want to be able to view my todo list on my phone.
Competitive Analysis: Todoist: Feature-rich, but complex for simple use cases.
Any.do: Clean interface, but requires a subscription for full functionality.
Google Tasks: Simple and integrated with Google ecosystem, but lacks advanced features.
Microsoft To Do: Integrated with Microsoft ecosystem, offers collaboration features.
TickTick: Offers Pomodoro timer and habit tracking, potentially overwhelming for simple todo lists.
Remember The Milk: Powerful features, but the UI feels dated.

Requirement Analysis: The core requirements are straightforward: adding, deleting, and marking tasks as complete. Data persistence is crucial for usability. A simple and intuitive interface is essential to avoid feature bloat and ensure ease of use. Responsiveness will allow users to access the todo list on various devices.
Requirement Pool: Implement data persistence (e.g., using local storage or a simple database).
UI Design draft: Simple, clean design. A text input field for adding tasks, a list to display tasks with checkboxes for completion, and delete buttons for each task. Tasks should be clearly displayed with a visual indication of their completion status (e.g., strikethrough). Layout should be mobile-first and adapt to larger screens.
